panels.description: Tokens consumed per time bucket, grouped by normalized model family and summed across input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation token classes. Aggregated with max_over_time, not increase: these counters are cumulative PER SESSION (every series carries session_id) and expire 15m after their last sample, so increase() would treat a short session's first sample as its baseline and undercount. See OTL-75. OTL-82 recording-rules round (Ryan-directed): each point is the amount accrued IN THAT INTERVAL BUCKET, computed as accum(t) - accum(t - $__interval) against a genuinely monotonic, forward-latching Prometheus recording rule (ai:tokens_accum:sum / ai:cost_usd_accum:sum -- see provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml's "ai-canonical-running-total" group) instead of re-deriving the delta from the raw per-session counter at query time on every dashboard load. Because it's ONE exact series subtracted from itself (not two independent max_over_time evaluations of a volatile raw counter, which is what produced OTL-82-r4's measured 3-4% token / 6-15% cost reconciliation error), the sum of all rendered bucket deltas telescopes EXACTLY to accum(end) - accum(start - $__interval) -- no reconciliation error, by construction rather than by measurement, so the legend Total now agrees with the stat tile for the same window. Legend still shows Latest / Peak / Total (Grafana's built-in lastNotNull / max / sum reducers -- rendered as "Last *" / "Max" / "Total"). HONEST LIMITATION: the accumulator only knows about activity from the moment it was deployed forward -- a dashboard window that starts before the rule's own deployment reads Total as everything captured since deployment, not the true pre-deployment history (the same characteristic every other canonical ai:* recording rule in this file already has). See the OTL-82/OTL-83 PR thread for the live-proof numbers.

Each model and fleet total reconciles to native spend. Aggregated with max_over_time, not increase: these counters are cumulative PER SESSION (every series carries session_id) and expire 15m after their last sample, so increase() would treat a short session's first sample as its baseline and undercount. See OTL-75. OTL-82-r4 (Ryan-directed redesign): each point is now the amount accrued IN THAT INTERVAL BUCKET, not a running total -- computed per-series as clamp_min(this bucket's max - the previous bucket's max, 0), summed across series (avoids increase()/rate(), which this repo's OTL-75 note already flagged as unreliable on these per-session counters -- max_over_time keeps that guarantee, applied per-bucket instead of over a growing window). Legend now shows Latest / Peak / Total (Grafana's built-in lastNotNull / max / sum reducers -- Grafana does not allow renaming a legend calc's own column header, so the table literally reads "Last *" / "Max" / "Total"). Total is now a legitimate window sum, not the double-counting bug OTL-82 originally fixed. Measured live against the stat tile's raw total for the same window (job="otel-collector", no template-var filtering, $__interval=2m over a live 2h window, real fleet churn): tokens matched within about 3-4% (undercount); cost was off by roughly 6-15% depending on bucket width (overcount, worse at narrow buckets, improving toward ~6% by 10-15m buckets) -- not a tight guarantee, the honest tolerance for this construction on a live, high-churn multi-session dataset. panels.description: Cross-provider token volume via the ai:tokens:sum canonical recording rule (provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml): provider=anthropic (real Claude, model!~"^glm"), provider=glm (model=~"^glm", split out 2026-08-24 for OTL-81), provider=openai (Codex_Desktop/app-server native token metric only — codex_exec headless emits no Prometheus token-usage series, see the recording-rules.yml header note). provider=qwen is a structural placeholder — its series appear automatically once Qwen telemetry exists (OTL-80). OTL-82-r4 (Ryan-directed redesign): each point is now the amount accrued IN THAT INTERVAL BUCKET, not a running total -- computed per-series as clamp_min(this bucket's max - the previous bucket's max, 0), summed across series (avoids increase()/rate(), which this repo's OTL-75 note already flagged as unreliable on these per-session counters -- max_over_time keeps that guarantee, applied per-bucket instead of over a growing window). options.content:
### Claude Code emits no metric this section could plot

A tok/s **percentile distribution** per model (mirroring the Latency section above) needs a per-request pairing of *tokens generated* and *time taken*, exposed as a histogram Grafana can run `histogram_quantile()` against. Checked the full live `claude_code_*` metric surface (2026-08-25) -- it does not exist:

- `claude_code_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket` -- a duration histogram, labeled `model`/`le`. No token count attached to any one request.
- `claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total` -- a counter, labeled `model`/`type` (input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation). No duration attached, and it is a *cumulative counter*, not a per-request event -- there is no way to recover "tokens produced in the same request that took N seconds" from it.

These two metrics are never joined at the per-request level anywhere in the exported telemetry, so there is no way to derive a real percentile distribution of tokens/second from what's on this stack today -- only a coarse aggregate (`rate(tokens_total) / rate(duration_seconds_sum)` over a window), which is a single blended number, not a P50-P99 distribution, and would misrepresent the ticket's ask if shown here as if it were one.

**What would light this up:** Claude Code's OTel exporter would need to either (a) emit a genuine per-request `tokens_per_second` (or `output_tokens` + `duration`) histogram, or (b) attach an output-token count as an attribute on the same span/event that already carries `api_request_duration`, so the two can be correlated per-request instead of only as independent aggregates. Neither exists in the current Claude Code telemetry surface -- this is an upstream instrumentation gap, not something this dashboard's queries can work around.
